author: hattrill
body: [QuickGO-annotations-1777384194944-20260428.tsv](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27167903/QuickGO-annotations-1777384194944-20260428.tsv) @LiNiMGI - I am looking at neuroblast term annotations as there are some issues to untangle with the way that arthropods and vertebrates use the term 'neuroblast' In vertebrates. A postmitotic cell that does not divide further. Develops into a neuron after a migration phase. In flies, neuroblasts are neural stem cells. Mitotic, self-renewing and produce ganglion mother cells, which differentiates into neurons or glial cells. But in the ontology division and differentiation are tangled. I think that the solution is for fly to move all their neuroblast differentiation annotations to the asymmetric neuroblast division branch or to other differentation/dev terms and for mice to move the neuroblast proliferation annotations to another proliferation term under 'neural precursor cell proliferation'. And then we can do some name changes to make sure that they are not confused and that they map to the correct term in the CL. I have attached a download of annotations from QuickGO under neuroblast proliferation for mouse (annotations to these terms seem to be largely/solely used by flies and mice). Could you check some of them against the publications and the ontology to see if there are more suitable terms. In summary, the solution looks like: all division ones go to fly and we change the CL map to neuroblast (sensu Nematoda and Protostomia) and all the neuroblast differentiation terms to map to neuroblast (sensu Vertebrata) and completely separate the branches and rename to avoid mistakes in the future. But, before I make the tickets for the ontology changes and annotation migrations, I wanted to check if you think this is the correct path.
title: Review mouse annotations under "neuroblast proliferation"

author: cindyJax
body:
I do not know where the definition of vertebrate neuroblast listed above comes from, but it's not quite accurate. 
1) High doublecortin (DCX) and PSA-NCAM expression is considered a marker for neuroblasts in vertebrates.  These cells are distinct from neural precursor cells (NPC) based on level DCX expression and the presence of nestin expression in NPCs, not neuroblasts.  Re-annotating from neuroblast terms to NPC terms would be wrong.   
2) Migrating neuroblasts do proliferate, although not as substantially as in flies  PMID: 35084970, PMID: 17376977.

author: hattrill
body:
thanks @cindyJax 
The definition comes from https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK10993/
"The progenitor cells of the neural tube are known as neural precursor cells. These precursors are dividing stem cells that produce more precursors and, eventually, nondividing neuroblasts that differentiate into neurons."
But if migrating neuroblasts divide, my suggestion falls down. Will examine the 'sensu' route instead and get back with a suggestion (will be next week before I can get to this)
